x: Sourcegull is a self-hosted code search and code intelligence platform for GitLab, GitHub and Gitea. It runs as one binary with PostgreSQL as its only dependency, and installs with Docker or a Helm chart.

Install: Docker Compose, Kubernetes (Helm), S3 blob storage, first sign-in and connecting GitLab, GitHub or Gitea. Configuration: environment variables, site configuration, user and organization settings, encryption keys, database pools, configuration as code (resources and global settings files). Permissions and sign-in: sign-in providers, repository permissions from GitLab, roles, access tokens, access requests, SCIM and audit events. Monitoring(observability/): Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alerts, with the next steps for each alert ). Upgrades: Docker Compose, Helm chart.

Search: the query language, search contexts, saved searches and search jobs. Code navigation: precise (SCIP), syntactic and search-based navigation, auto-indexing and file ranking. Bulk changes: bulk change specs, running them on executors or locally, and merge requests on GitLab. Other features: rendered Markdown and READMEs, trends, watches, notebooks, code ownership, compute, usage analytics, outbound webhooks and site administration. AI agents (MCP): the MCP server at /.api/mcp and how to connect coding agents.

Architecture: roles, storage, gRPC, repo node partitioning, the search index and a map of the crates. Development: the Docker development environment, tests, browser checks, benchmarks and conventions. Roadmap: planned work, with the design and the definition of done for each item.

With configuration as code, the database holds only what users create; restoring an instance from git and an empty database loses users' tokens, settings and content, not the instance's configuration. Results are ordered by score within one search. A file scores by its best match: a match on a symbol definition counts most, then a whole-word match, then a partial match, with extra weight when every term matches and for matches in the file name. Keyword queries score with BM25 over their terms instead. Test, vendored and generated files are scored down. Ties are broken by the file's static rank from the code graph, shallower paths and the repository's rank.

When no precise data covers a position, Sourcegull searches for the symbol: definitions come from symbol search (tree-sitter symbol extraction for 19 languages), references from a case-sensitive whole-word text search, both narrowed to the file's language family. A worker job builds the reference graph of all precise indexes that serve each repository's default branch: files are nodes, and references between them (also across repositories) are weighted edges. It computes PageRank over this graph and stores a static rank per file. Repo nodes write the ranks into the search index at the next full build, and search uses them to break ties between equally good matches, so central, widely used files come first. The ranking is on by default (codeIntelRanking.documentReferenceCountsEnabled) and has no effect until precise indexes exist.

PostgreSQL (16 or newer) holds all durable state and also does the jobs often given to other services: Job queues (pgqueue): one table per queue, dequeued with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, with heartbeats, retries with backoff and a resetter for jobs whose worker died. Notifications (LISTEN/NOTIFY) wake up workers and propagate site configuration, permission changes and the repo routing table. Every subscriber polls as a fallback, since notifications are not durable. Leader election: advisory locks, or Kubernetes Lease objects (SOURCEGULLLEADERBACKEND=kubernetes). Each repository belongs to one repo node, chosen by rendezvous hashing of its name over the node list in SOURCEGULLREPONODES. Every process computes the same assignment, so web and worker route requests without a lookup service. The assignment is stored per repository and published with NOTIFY when it changes. Sourcegull has its own index format (crates/index-format), built by crates/indexer on the repo nodes and queried by crates/search-exec. The rest of the system reaches it only through the SearchIndex trait (crates/search/src/index.rs). Shards. A shard file holds one repository's indexed branches: by default the default branch, plus those listed in search.index.branches and those selected by search.index.recentBranches, up to 64 in all. Executors run untrusted work (indexers, bulk change steps) outside the server processes. They poll the web role's queues (codeintel, batches), send heartbeats, and report each job as completed, failed or errored (errored jobs are retried). The Docker runtime runs each step as a container with optional memory, CPU and network limits; the Kubernetes runtime runs each job as a Kubernetes Job with configurable namespace, runtime class, node selector, tolerations and resources. Executor secrets (site- or namespace-level) are injected as environment variables.
